AL.hint: Red with a black double-headed eagle. Montenegro's eagle is gold, with a gold border.
AL.funFact: Albania has over 170,000 concrete bunkers built during its communist era.

AD.hint: Blue, yellow, red vertical like Chad and Romania, but with a coat of arms in the middle.
AD.funFact: Andorra has two co-princes: the President of France and the Bishop of Urgell in Spain.

AT.hint: Red-white-red horizontal. Latvia is darker maroon with a thinner white stripe.
AT.funFact: Austria's flag is one of the oldest in the world, with legends dating it to 1191.

BY.hint: Red over green with a red-and-white folk-embroidery strip down the flagpole side.
BY.funFact: Belarus shares the ancient Białowieża Forest with Poland, home of the European bison.

BE.hint: Black, yellow, red vertical: Germany's colours standing up.
BE.funFact: Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.

BA.hint: Blue with a yellow triangle and a diagonal line of white stars, some cut off at the edges.
BA.funFact: The triangle's three corners are said to stand for the country's three main peoples.

BG.hint: White, green, red horizontal. Hungary has red on top instead of white.
BG.funFact: Bulgaria's 'Valley of Roses' produces a large share of the world's rose oil for perfume.

HR.hint: Red, white, blue stripes with a red-and-white checkerboard shield in the middle.
HR.funFact: The necktie (cravat) is named after Croatian soldiers who wore knotted scarves in the 1600s.

CY.hint: White with a copper-orange map of the island above two green olive branches.
CY.funFact: Cyprus was famous for copper in ancient times, which is why the map on the flag is copper-coloured.

CZ.hint: White over red with a blue triangle. The Philippines adds a sun and stars in its triangle.
CZ.funFact: Czechs drink more beer per person than any other country.

DK.hint: Red with a white off-centre cross: the original Nordic cross.
DK.funFact: Denmark's flag, the Dannebrog, is the oldest national flag still in continuous use.

EE.funFact: Estonia was the first country to offer internet voting nationwide, starting in 2005.

FI.hint: White with a blue Nordic cross, like snow and lakes.

FR.hint: Blue, white, red vertical. Italy swaps the blue for green.
FR.funFact: France is the most visited country in the world.

DE.hint: Black, red, gold horizontal. Belgium uses similar colours vertically.

GR.hint: Nine blue and white stripes with a white cross in the blue corner.
GR.funFact: The nine stripes are said to match the nine syllables of 'Freedom or Death' in Greek.

HU.hint: Red, white, green horizontal: Italy's colours lying down.
HU.funFact: The Rubik's Cube was invented by Hungarian Ernő Rubik in 1974.

IS.hint: Blue with a red cross outlined in white. Norway is the colour-swap: red with a blue cross.
IS.funFact: Iceland has no army and is regularly ranked the world's most peaceful country.

IE.hint: Green, white, orange vertical, with green at the flagpole. Ivory Coast is the reverse.
IE.funFact: Green stands for Irish Catholics, orange for Protestants, and white for peace between them.

IT.hint: Green, white, red vertical. Mexico adds an eagle; France swaps green for blue.
IT.funFact: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country.

LV.hint: Dark maroon-red with a thin white stripe, darker and thinner than Austria's.
LV.funFact: Latvia's red-white-red design is mentioned in a 13th-century chronicle.

LI.hint: Blue over red with a small gold crown in the top-left corner.
LI.funFact: The crown was added after the 1936 Olympics revealed that Liechtenstein's flag was identical to Haiti's.

LT.hint: Yellow, green, red horizontal, like a traffic light with green in the middle.
LT.funFact: Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare independence, in 1990.

LU.hint: Red, white, light blue. The Netherlands is the same but with a darker blue.
LU.funFact: Luxembourg is the world's only remaining Grand Duchy.

MT.hint: White and red halves with a small grey George Cross in the top-left.
MT.funFact: King George VI awarded the George Cross to the whole island for its bravery in World War II.

MD.hint: Blue, yellow, red vertical like Romania, but with an eagle coat of arms in the middle.
MD.funFact: Moldova's Mileștii Mici cellars hold the world's largest wine collection, nearly 2 million bottles.

MC.hint: Red over white, the same colours as Indonesia but squarer. Poland is white over red.
MC.funFact: Monaco is the world's second-smallest country, smaller than New York's Central Park.

ME.hint: Red with a gold border and a gold double-headed eagle. Albania's eagle is black.
ME.funFact: Montenegro uses the euro even though it isn't in the EU.

NL.hint: Red, white, blue horizontal. Luxembourg's blue is lighter; Russia goes white-blue-red.
NL.funFact: There are more bicycles than people in the Netherlands.

MK.hint: Red with a yellow sun whose eight rays stretch all the way to the edges.
MK.funFact: Mother Teresa was born in Skopje, North Macedonia's capital.

NO.hint: Red with a blue Nordic cross outlined in white. Iceland is the colour-swap.
NO.funFact: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo every year.

PL.hint: White over red. Indonesia and Monaco are red over white.
PL.funFact: Marie Curie, the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, was born in Warsaw.

PT.hint: Green and red with a yellow armillary sphere (a globe-like instrument) and shield on the dividing line.
PT.funFact: Portugal and England have the world's oldest active alliance, dating from 1373.

RO.hint: Blue, yellow, red vertical, almost identical to Chad. Romania's blue is a little lighter.
RO.funFact: Bucharest's Palace of the Parliament is one of the heaviest buildings in the world.

RU.hint: White, blue, red horizontal. Slovenia and Slovakia add a coat of arms.

SM.hint: White over light blue with a coat of arms showing three towers.
SM.funFact: Founded in 301 AD, San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic.

RS.hint: Red, blue, white stripes (Russia upside down) with a double-headed eagle shield.
RS.funFact: Serbia is one of the world's biggest raspberry exporters.

SK.hint: White, blue, red with a shield showing a white double cross on three blue hills.
SK.funFact: Slovakia makes more cars per person than any other country.

SI.hint: White, blue, red with a small shield showing a white mountain (Triglav) and three yellow stars.
SI.funFact: More than half of Slovenia is covered by forest.

ES.hint: Red, yellow, red with a thick yellow middle and a coat of arms near the flagpole.
ES.funFact: Spain's national anthem has no official lyrics.

SE.hint: Blue with a yellow Nordic cross.
SE.funFact: Sweden's 'right to roam' lets anyone walk and camp on most land, even if it's privately owned.

CH.hint: A square red flag with a white plus-shaped cross. It's one of only two square national flags.
CH.funFact: The Red Cross symbol is the Swiss flag with its colours reversed.

UA.hint: Blue over yellow: the sky above wheat fields.
UA.funFact: Ukraine is the largest country lying entirely within Europe.

GB.hint: The Union Jack: England's red cross, Scotland's white X and Ireland's red X on blue.
GB.funFact: The Union Jack appears in the corner of other flags too, like Australia, New Zealand, Fiji and Tuvalu.

VA.hint: A square flag: yellow and white halves with crossed gold and silver keys under the papal crown.
VA.funFact: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, at just 0.44 km².
